validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed, high confidence — this is the well-documented Eni (op, 50%) / TotalEnergies (50%) Cronos (Block 6, Cyprus EEZ, >3 tcf in place) fast-track export tieback to Egypt. Independent corroboration: Eni press release 2025-02-17 (HGA with Egypt+Cyprus; gas 'transported and processed in existing Zohr facilities' then Damietta LNG); Offshore Magazine 2025-02-17; Politis (Cyprus) 2026-02-27 explicitly: gas to flow 'through a 90km subsea pipeline' to Zohr facilities, first gas H1 2028; Cyprus Mail 2026-05-23 (DPP approved 19 May 2026, FID pending); commercial HTPA/tolling/tariff agreements signed Oct 2025 (MEES via Egypt Oil & Gas 2025-10-26). NOT a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: gas transmission — correct (offshore export trunk). DUPLICATE: none — distinct from P0473 Cyprus-Egypt (Aphrodite/Block 12, Chevron, ~310 km to Damietta/Idku) and from the Israel-Egypt lines P3620/P3657. Note for discovery, not dup: the same project family includes a separate NEW onshore pipeline from Zohr's Port Said plant direct to Damietta LNG bypassing the national grid (MEES) — GEM has no row for that; do not fold it into P7597. ATTRIBUTION CAVEATS: (1) sheet EndCountryOrArea is misspelled 'Egypy'; (2) End=Port Said is loose — the 90 km figure matches the Cronos->Zohr offshore tie-in distance (MEES/Politis), while Cronos->Port Said onshore would be roughly 250+ km (Zohr is 190 km north of Port Said); onward Zohr->Port Said transport is via existing 30-inch Zohr line, so P7597's new-build endpoint is the Zohr offshore hub. LENGTH 90 km: corroborated by Politis 2026-02-27 (verifier-passed) matching the original Asharq figure; one secondary strand says ~110 km — minor conflict, keep 90.
